**About BLAST

**BLAST is a global competitive entertainment company working with some of the world's biggest game publishers, brands and entertainment properties to create world-class esports and live entertainment experiences.

We operate globally across multiple ecosystems, delivering everything from large-scale arena events and broadcasts to digital products and content.

Our values — Make it Bold, Make it Together and Make it Happen — shape how we work, collaborate and deliver.

**Welcome to the Global Mobility Team at BLAST!

**At BLAST, we bring people together - across borders, stages, and time zones. Now we're looking for a Global Mobility Consultant to join our team and help us ensure that our people can thrive wherever in the world our events take them.

You'll be part of a small but passionate team of colleagues, working closely with People and Culture, Travel, Finance, Legal, and Live Events to build and run a world-class mobility framework that supports BLAST's global growth.

**What You'll Be Doing - Your Impact

**As our new Global Mobility Consultant, you'll make it easier for people to move across borders with confidence - whether they're employees, freelancers, or part of our extended network.

**Your key responsibilities include:

**

• Acting as an advisor on international hires and postings

• Coordinating with P&O, Payroll, and external vendors (legal, tax, relocation)

• Managing work permit and visa applications, incl. compliance and documentation

• Providing guidance to cross-border employees and freelancers

• Drafting invitation and support letters

• Supporting the expansion of our Global Mobility hub and processes

• Liaising with specialised legal counsels as needed

• Handling admin tasks like budget tracking, PO creation, and updating WIPS

• Taking on other ad hoc tasks as the need arises - flexibility is key!

• Managing portfolio-wide shared services scope across key global operational regions

• Ensuring close cross-departmental collaboration with Travel, People Operations, and Legal

• Serving as the primary coordination point for all international mobility queries and escalation

• Providing dedicated talent and event-specific support for global tournament operations

• Driving process scalability and documentation across global mobility workflows

• High-Volume Event Scaling, managing visa and immigration logistics for large-scale international tournaments involving up to 400 personnel per event (including Third-Country Nationals, employees, and freelancers)

• Reviewing agreements with local partners and drafting special clauses regarding visa support, including negotiating terms, intervention costs, sourcing local vendors/counsel, and handling contract negotiations, term reviews, and cost analysis

• Direct interaction and coordination with immigration authorities, government departments, and local regulatory bodies, rather than solely liaising with external legal counsel

• Local Entity Compliance & Corporate Service Provider Coordination, overseeing local corporate compliance requirements such as employer registrations, and local tax/social security considerations

**Who You Are - To Succeed In This Role

**You're an excellent communicator, a proactive problem-solver, and a trusted partner to your colleagues. You thrive in a dynamic environment, love the details, and care about creating smooth experiences for people on the move.

**Requirements

****Experience:

**

• A degree in HR, Business Administration, Legal - or equivalent experience

• 3+ years of experience with international assignments and cross-border employment particularly in relation to North America and Asia

• Strong understanding of mobility processes and compliance

• Solid experience working with Excel (e.g. data management, formulas, reporting) Proficiency in tools like Smartsheet, Google Sheets, and AI and automation tools and platforms

• Experience providing team leadership, guidance, and mentorship within a small team environment

• Previous background in the sports, entertainment, or fast-paced live events industry, given the scale of international tournaments

• Demonstrated flexibility, interpretation, and creativity in navigating complex or ambiguous visa regulations across global destinations lacking standardized visa categories

• Experience with budget tracking, cost control, PO creation, and managing financial considerations related to global mobility and travel

• Proven ability to manage high-pressure situations, tight event deadlines, and complex logistical escalations independently

• Strong cross functional stakeholder engagement skills to coordinate seamlessly across all the internal Blast teams as well as external vendors

• Willingness to work flexible hours during major events or travel occasionally between the London and Copenhagen offices

**Benefits

****What We Offer - Life at BLAST

**

• At BLAST, you'll join a creative, collaborative, and international environment where no two days are the same. We're proud of our culture - one where people are seen, heard, and encouraged to bring ideas forward

**Here's a glimpse of what you'll get:

**

• A fast-paced and supportive workplace

• Great colleagues

• Flexible working conditions

• Centrally located office in Copenhagen

• Personal and professional development opportunities

• Friday bars, social events, and access to world-class esports action

Ready to join us?

We're excited to meet you. Apply now and help us shape the future of Global Mobility at BLAST

jobs.occupation: International Customer Success Manager for a Copenhagen grid-tech start-up
jobs.description:
Are you a customer-facing project manager who thrives on paving the way to success for B2B customers? Do you speak fluent German and English – and perhaps Spanish/Italian? Do you see yourself in a fast-growing start-up with an international team that is securing critical electrical infrastructure?

Then you could be Oktogrid’s new Customer Success Manager!

About Oktogrid

Oktogrid helps secure critical infrastructure by bringing power transformers online for higher reliability and a more sustainable operation. Oktogrid’s sensor solution significantly accelerates the path to getting access to the right data to support operators with the necessary insights for their decision-making.

Founded in 2020. Oktogrid has the continued backing of major European investors, including ABB Electrification and Elewit Ventures, and works with a wide range of grid operators across Europe. The company has 14 employees, most of whom are based at the Copenhagen office, with sales colleagues based in Germany and the Netherlands. Oktogrid also works with an international development team. English is the company language.

About the role

Reporting directly to the CEO, who also heads up sales, you will ensure that Oktogrid’s customers get off to a strong start and support them on their journey as they continue to benefit of the value from the solution. As the Customer Success Manager, you will follow each new customer closely throughout the first 3-9 months – from installation workshops to confidently onboarding onto the Transformer Intelligence Platform.

You will remain their trusted point of contact for the entire customer journey, while your experience in project coordination will ensure that the right expertise from your colleagues is involved whenever needed. Your job is not to acquire new customers, but to build strong relationships with existing ones, identify new needs and plant the seeds for further collaboration. You will be based at the Copenhagen office, with occasional travel.

Your primary responsibilities:

• 
Running a structured onboarding process for new customers – from project kick-off workshops to onboarding onto the Transformer Intelligence Platform

• 
Following up closely with customers and holding regular check-ins to ensure that they get the value they expect

• 
Owning a portfolio of Danish and international customers, with a focus on German-speaking markets

• 
Engaging with a rich map of stakeholders within each customer organisation – for example, the operations managers in each region – so that the solution becomes part of their day-to-day work

• 
Bringing in Oktogrid’s technical experts when customers need in-depth answers about transformers, deeper data analytics or software integrations

• 
Identifying new needs and opportunities – such as additional analytics modules and reports – and passing them on to the product and operations teams

• 
Capturing customer feedback and success stories for Product and Marketing

• 
Building and continuously improving Oktogrid’s Customer Success process and playbook

About you

A background in utilities or within energy is a plus, but not a requirement – Oktogrid’s experts are at hand when in-depth expertise is needed. What matters most is that you are excellent at building trust, maintaining close dialogue with customers and picking up on when to involve your extended team at Oktogrid. Having previously worked within energy, telecoms, IT, SaaS or other B2B industries in which you have delivered complex solutions to large customers are relevant fields of experience. We envisage that you have:

• 
5-10 years’ experience in Customer Success or related customer-facing roles with B2B customers

• 
Experience of working with structured customer processes – ideally gained in a medium-sized company where you have had broad responsibility

• 
Experience in delivering complex solutions and managing long-term customer relationships, rather than having ambitions of driving transactional sales

• 
Technical understanding and the ability to explain complex solutions clearly to expert as well as non-expert stakeholders

• 
A proactive approach – you bring your own ideas to the table and take ownership of improving the way things are done

• 
Genuine curiosity about customers’ needs – you spot opportunities that create further value for them

• 
The drive to succeed in a fast-growing start-up as part of a high-performing, international team – and a preference for working from the office in close contact with customers and colleagues

• 
Fluent in German and English, written and spoken. Spanish and Italian would be a strong advantage, as many customers prefer to communicate in their own language

• 
Experience with utilities and an understanding of asset management practices would be an advantage, but is not a requirement

• 
A valid permit to live and work in Denmark (EU/EEA citizenship or a Danish work permit)

Oktogrid offers

• 
A key role with real influence in a company actively driving a meaningful climate impact

• 
Office-based work with flexible working hours, the option of working from home one day a week and a partly paid company lunch scheme every day

• 
A modern office space in Copenhagen at the border between Vesterbro and Frederiksberg, located close to green areas and a vibrant hub where innovation meets great city culture

• 
A salary based on qualifications, and a company-wide bonus scheme

Interested?

Apply as soon as possible by clicking the application button and uploading your CV and, if you wish, a cover letter, both in English.

If you have any questions, please contact Martin Nielsen, Headhunter & Partner at Landau Headhunting, on +45 8122 8180. Landau Headhunting is managing the recruitment process on behalf of Oktogrid, so please direct all enquiries to us. We will review applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.

We look forward to hearing from you! Read more about Oktogrid at https://oktogrid.io

_Do you want to be the commercial anchor between our customers and our product offerings in our Heat/Cooling Division? Do you enjoy connecting customer needs with commercial opportunities and technical possibilities? Do you want to help shape smart metering products and solutions that accelerate the green transition?

**Here Is What The Job Entails

**As our Senior Commercial Product Manager for Hardware Solutions, you will work cross functionally on product lifecycle optimization of our Heating and Cooling solutions to align product development with market demands, customer needs, and revenue goals. To do so, you will be responsible for driving the commercial aspects of our product portfolio, including product launches and lifecycle management.

More specifically, you will be:

• Managing the product lifecycle from idea to end-of-life

• Driving product discovery and portfolio optimization projects in close collaboration with our customers, Sales and Marketing

• Owning the business case and commercial roadmap for hardware products, including pricing, to ensure profitability and market fit

• Working with colleagues across the organization, training Sales and Customer Support to succeed

• Challenging status quo to ensure continuity of commercially viable solutions

You will be at the forefront of decision-making, steering the direction of our products and solutions. In this role, you will have the mandate to act, and the responsibility needed to make impactful decisions that help our customers adapt to a more sustainable future.

**Meet your future team

**With direct reference to Senior Manager, Commercial Product Management, you will become part of a team of highly skilled colleagues who work every day to bring smart metering solutions and services to our markets. The Commercial Product Management team combines strong commercial capabilities with a solid technical understanding of our solutions to drive profitability and help our customers succeed in energy efficiency and the green transition.

The team is part of the Product Management organization for Heat/Cooling products and solutions and brings together colleagues with strong technical, commercial and strategic expertise. This diversity helps us achieve a high level of quality and challenge status quo, which is something we value highly in our department.

**Less About Us, More About You

**We are looking for an ambitious and passionate colleague who brings a profound drive to deliver winning and value-adding solutions to the green transition. You have a natural drive and an “outside in” perspective in everything you do. Ideally, you bring experience of working in a matrix, from an international setting.

To succeed in this role, we envision that you:

• Have experience working at the intersection of customers, business, technology and products, driving decisions across functions and organizational levels

• Have a great commercial understanding combined with a high technical interest – or vice versa

• Can apply Product Management disciplines to translate customer and market insights into successful products

• Are an effective communicator who excels in building and maintaining strong relationships both internally and with customers

• Can translate technical information to a broad audience

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

**We are more than an ordinary workplace

**We cherish the good colleagueship which we all contribute to, the only limit is your engagement. As we are a big organization you are bound to find one or more colleagues who share the same interest as you. This might be in our board game club, on our cycling team, during our yearly summer festival, or on the padel court. For example, our Team lead, Service Delivery is also our volunteer padel instructor while one of our Software Test Engineers run weekly spinning classes.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Department: Operations (Engineering Services & Customer Support)

Location: Copenhagen

**Description

**At Factbird, we help manufacturers see what’s really happening on their lines, so they can make better, faster decisions. Our plug-and-play hardware and cloud platform turn live production data into clear insights, and we’re scaling fast across sites, teams, and countries.

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior IoT Solutions Engineer to join Engineering Services, the team that takes on the technical problems that fall outside what our product and Support handle today. You’ll look at a PLC, a sensor, or a 20-year-old CNC and work out how to get its data into Factbird. Sales and Support turn to you when the answer is “it depends,” and you turn that into a clear yes, no, or “here’s how.” Then you write it down so the next person doesn’t need to ask.

****About the role

**Engineering Services solves the hardest technical problems, documents them, and shares the knowledge, so Factbird gets smarter and the same problem doesn’t come back. You’ll answer feasibility questions before deals close, design and build custom solutions, and fix the cross-domain problems no other team can place.

**

The team mission we are on: Engineering Services is a small team of experts finding solutions to a wide variety of challenges. In pre-sales we are supporting our AE's and Solution Consultants with feasibility testing the most complex customer setups or requirements. Often directly with the customers and their technical teams. In post-sales we collaborate with Cloud, FW and HW teams, and build and support a range of custom solutions. Our core mission is to increase documentation, standardization and empowering our colleagues in both pre- and post-sales roles to server the customers in the most technical cases.

**What You'll Do

**

• Answer feasibility questions from Sales: can we connect this machine, PLC, or sensor, and how

• Design and build custom solutions: logic boxes, signal converters, IO-Link modules, EDGE flows, and Factbird® powered by OMRON NX1 programs that fill gaps the cloud platform can’t handle yet.

• Design the integration: map the customer’s OT/IT environment and plan the data sources, tag structures, transformations, and security.

• Root cause troubleshooting in live production. Smaller share of time, highest stakes

• Document everything you build and fix: Solution Records, runbooks, and wiring guides for customers and internal teams, clear enough that someone else can pick it up. Version and back up every configuration.

• Bench-test hardware before it ships, test the full data flow end to end (including failure recovery and restarts), and hand hardware to Logistics with a clear packing list.

• Integrate customer systems through Kepware, Ignition, OPC UA, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and Node-RED.

• Share what you know: help Support, Solution Consultants, and Hardware handle more on their own.

• Streamline as you go: spot repeat work and clunky processes, and fix them or flag them. Build templates and scripts that make the next delivery faster.

• Turn repeat workarounds into product input with a business case, so the workaround can disappear.

• Join customer and prospect calls as the technical voice alongside Solution Consultants and Account Managers.

**About you

**You’re an experienced industrial automation engineer, as happy with a screwdriver as with a terminal. You know how factories work, and you’re comfortable saying “not directly, but here’s the route.”

You document like the next person depends on it, because they do. You can’t leave a clunky process alone: you always have an eye on how to make things simpler and more repeatable.

You’re flexible and self-directed: you take a high level of accountability and ownership. You can prioritize and deliver without daily supervision, and you troubleshoot systematically when things get ambiguous. The work changes week to week, and the team’s shape will keep evolving as Factbird grows. You’re happy to do what’s needed today while helping move things in a more scalable direction.

You love being the expert, but you equally love teaching others and making the teams around you smarter. And most of all, you care about making the answer simple for whoever asked.

Requirements:

• A bachelor's degree in automation, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• At least 5 years in industrial automation or controls engineering, including hands-on work on the shop floor (7+ years preferred).

• Hands-on PLC experience with at least one major vendor, e.g. Siemens, Omron, or Rockwell/Allen-Bradley.

• Solid understanding of industrial protocols, e.g. OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, MQTT.

• Working knowledge of sensors and signals, like digital, analog (4–20 mA, 0–10 V), IO-Link, PNP/NPN, and energy metering.

• Root cause analysis across hardware, networks, and software in live production environments.

• Field experience commissioning or troubleshooting equipment in live plants.

• Comfortable troubleshooting site networks, e.g. IP setup, routers, SIMs, and firewalls.

• A clear communicator in English who can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

• A strong documentation habit: when you build it, you write it down.

**Why Factbird?

**People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We’ll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we’ll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We’d love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Khristel, our Global Talent Acquisition & People Operations Lead at **khma@factbird.com

**_At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

__All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

_We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

Global Service Specialist - DO/Emico, Flotation PCV, DSG-3

**Job Title: Global Service Specialist – DO/EIMCO, Flotation, PCV, DSG

**Position Summary

**FLS is seeking a highly skilled and professional Global Service Specialist to support the erection, installation, pre‑commissioning, commissioning, and operational startup of commercial and industrial separation equipment. This role focuses primarily on mechanical work and Installation & Commissioning (I&C) activities for thickeners and flotation cells, with additional responsibility for equipment such as clarifiers, cyclones, pumps, reactors, and agitated tanks.

The Global Service Specialist serves as FLS’s primary onsite representative and is responsible for delivering high‑quality technical service, maintaining strong customer relationships, and ensuring safe and efficient project execution. This position requires extensive international travel and the ability to work independently under demanding conditions.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Execute onsite erection, installation, alignment, and commissioning of mechanical systems and I&C activities for thickeners, flotation cells, and related separation equipment.

• Lead pre‑commissioning and commissioning processes to ensure equipment meets design, safety, and performance requirements.

• Support operational startup, troubleshooting, and optimization of equipment performance.

• Conduct inspections, testing, calibration, and verification of mechanical and control‑related systems.

• Coordinate onsite project activities, schedules, and resources to ensure timely completion.

• Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and project management teams to resolve technical issues.

• Prepare accurate and professional documentation, including installation records, commissioning reports, and service summaries.

• Maintain compliance with all safety, quality, and regulatory standards.

• Serve as the primary onsite point of contact for customers, providing training, guidance, and technical support.

• Represent FLS with professionalism and integrity in all customer interactions.

**Qualifications

****Required

**

• Strong mechanical background with hands‑on experience in Installation & Commissioning (I&C) of industrial process equipment.

• Experience with thickeners, flotation cells, clarifiers, cyclones, pumps, reactors, or similar industrial equipment.

• Demonstrated ability to work independently and make informed decisions under pressure.

• Strong project management skills, including planning, coordination, and documentation.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce high‑quality technical reports.

• Ability and willingness to travel internationally up to 70% of the time.

• Professional demeanor with the ability to represent the company effectively onsite.

**Preferred

**

• Experience in commissioning or startup of industrial process systems.

• Background in mining, minerals processing, water treatment, or heavy industrial environments.

• Multilingual capabilities or experience working in multicultural settings.

• Ability to meet all medical and physical fitness requirements necessary to obtain work authorization for high‑altitude job sites.

**Competencies

**

• Technical proficiency in mechanical systems and industrial equipment

• Strong problem‑solving and decision‑making abilities

• Customer service orientation

• Professional communication and reporting skills

• Ability to perform effectively in high‑pressure environments

• Self‑motivation and independence in field operations

We offer all employees access to a dedicated recognition platform, empowering you to celebrate achievements, share appreciation and stay connected globally.

**Your impact begins here

**As Safety Surveillance Principal Process Specialist, you will keep Safety Surveillance ready for every audit and inspection, and make sure the way we monitor safety information keeps pace with legislation. You will be a highly visible process expert: leading our contribution to inspections, co-driving regulatory surveillance and shaping how we integrate processes after acquisitions. Your work keeps surveillance of Novo’s marketed and developmental products compliant, simpler and focused on the work that adds most value.

**What You’ll Bring

**You know drug safety from the inside, and you know what it takes to get an organisation ready for an inspection. You will also bring:

• A Master’s degree in Life Sciences, such as Pharmacy, Medicine, Veterinary Science or Biology, or a related field.

• At least 5–7 years of experience in pharmacovigilance, including supporting safety activities in clinical trials.

• Hands-on experience facilitating inspection set-ups, training colleagues and preparing an organisation for audits and inspections.

• Expertise in Safety Surveillance processes and an enterprise mindset: you understand the end-to-end process and can turn complex internal and external requirements into practical ways of working.

• A solid background in handling deviations and implementing process changes.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior internal stakeholders and external parties, and a collaborative mindset across functions and geographies.

• Resilience and a calm demeanour in a very busy environment, with the ability to multitask and prioritise your workload through complexity and challenge.

**Desirable, But Not Essential

**Experience in process management and project management.

**What You’ll Do

**You will be a recognised expert in key Safety Surveillance processes, helping the team work with greater simplicity and focus. The role covers a diverse range of tasks, and you could be part of an inspection from day one.

• Lead audits and inspections: coordinate Safety Surveillance contributions, prepare colleagues for interviews, ensure high-quality responses and keep oversight of findings and the associated corrective and preventive actions.

• Act as Process Expert for the signal management process and co-drive the Regulatory Surveillance process, ensuring full compliance with applicable legislation.

• Handle deviations and change requests in close collaboration with colleagues in Safety Surveillance and other relevant functions.

• Support integration and acquisition activities by helping integrate pharmacovigilance processes and systems following company or product acquisitions and mergers.

• Contribute to process improvement projects aligned with our strategic objectives, using your end-to-end view of Safety Surveillance.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join the Safety Surveillance Centre of Expertise, a team of five engaged and skilled colleagues within Safety Surveillance, and report to the Director of Safety Surveillance Centre of Expertise.

Safety Surveillance is a department within Global Patient Safety in Research & Development, with departments in Bangalore, India, and Boston, US. Together, we are globally accountable for surveillance of all safety information for Novo’s marketed products and products in development. We also handle safety label updates, Risk Management Plans and aggregate reports.

You will work closely with colleagues across Safety Surveillance and partner with Global Patient Safety, other headquarters functions and affiliates during audits and inspections. When processes need to change, you will bring the right people together, create clarity on what needs to happen and help the team move forward with pace.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will have real visibility as a process expert, and the opportunity to influence how Safety Surveillance works and make a lasting impact. You will be trusted to take ownership, encouraged to make your voice heard, and supported by colleagues who give honest feedback and never compromise on patient safety or quality.

The pace is high and the work is varied. Through process improvement projects and a broad range of tasks, you will build new skills and deepen your understanding of safety surveillance end to end.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,000 to

1,245,100 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

**Start now

**Your impact begins today, so apply by 17 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We are an equal opportunities employer and are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all applicants.

Über die Aufgabe

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join us in shaping the future of offshore wind. As our Traverse Equipment Owner, you will serve as the technical authority and lifecycle owner for traverse equipment used in offshore installation and servicing operations. You will be responsible for ensuring equipment performance, reliability, safety, and long-term value across a global fleet.

Working at the intersection of engineering, operations, project execution, suppliers, and management, you will play a key role in aligning diverse stakeholder needs and translating them into clear requirements, priorities, and improvement initiatives. Success in this role requires strong stakeholder management capabilities, sound technical judgement, and the ability to balance operational, commercial, and safety considerations.

You will drive the development of the traverse equipment roadmap, monitor fleet performance, and lead continuous improvement efforts throughout the equipment lifecycle. By fostering collaboration, standardization, and the adoption of new technologies, you will help ensure that our traverse solutions continue to support safe and efficient offshore operations worldwide.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Own the traverse equipment lifecycle, ensuring optimal performance, reliability, safety, and long-term business value.

• Translate operational and stakeholder needs into clear requirements, success criteria, and approved improvement initiatives.

• Develop and maintain the traverse equipment roadmap and prioritized backlog, including technology development and investment needs.

• Monitor fleet performance, assess incidents and lessons learned, and drive corrective actions, upgrades, and risk mitigation measures.

• Promote knowledge sharing, technical excellence, and the adoption of innovative technologies across the Equipment organization.

What You Bring

• An Engineering degree (Mechanical, Marine, Civil, Industrial, or similar) and at least 10 years of technical experience in equipment development, maintenance, or asset management within offshore wind or a comparable heavy-industry environment.

• Proven experience with traverse systems, lifting equipment, stabilization systems, motion control technologies, or other equipment used for offshore heavy-load handling.

• Demonstrated experience in equipment ownership, technical leadership, or lifecycle management of complex engineered products.

• Ability to convert operational challenges and user feedback into technical requirements, validation criteria, and improvement plans.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with a structured, proactive, and solution-oriented approach.

About the Team

You will join a global team responsible for the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of specialized offshore equipment. The team combines operational experience with engineering expertise to ensure equipment reliability, safety, and efficiency throughout its lifecycle. Together, we drive innovation, standardization, and best practices that support offshore wind projects worldwide.

Siemens Gamesa is part of Siemens Energy, a global leader in energy technology with a rich legacy of innovation spanning over 150 years. Together, we are committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. As a leading player in the wind industry and manufacturer of wind turbines, we are passionate about driving the energy transition and providing innovative solutions that meet the growing energy demand of the global community. At Siemens Gamesa, we are constantly seeking individuals to join our team and support our focus on energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Gamesa: https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/careers/working-with-us.html

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by multiple nationalities. We celebrate character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Rewards/Benefits

• Opportunities to work with a global team

• Medical benefits

• Remote/Flexible work

Are responsible for your product group’s buying budget, target margins and buying quantities – and for getting the right products delivered on time and to the agreed quality.

Lead the day-to-day dialogue and price negotiations with your suppliers, and follow up on their performance on quality, delivery precision and compliance.

Collection & orders

You are commercially minded and enjoy combining numbers, products and people. You take ownership of your area, keep track of the details without losing the big picture, and want a real say in what ends up in the collection. We imagine that you:

• 
Have 1–3 years of experience in buying, merchandising, sourcing or product development – ideally within fashion, footwear or lifestyle.

• 
Work in a structured way and take responsibility for your results from start to finish.

Can prioritise between several tasks and deadlines at once, and keep a cool head when plans change.

• 
Are interested in products, fashion and responsible production – knowledge of certifications or product safety requirements is a plus.

• 
We care more about your drive, commercial sense and willingness to learn than about ticking every box.

Real ownership of a product group and its suppliers at a growing international brand

• 
A clear path towards a Buyer role as your responsibilities and results develop

• 
Sparring and support from experienced colleagues in Buying & Supply Chain

• 
Insight into the full value chain – from design and sourcing to sales and delivery

• 
A warm and collaborative work environment where well-being, trust and professional development are priorities

Competitive salary and employment terms that match the role and your experience

Do you have experience configuring, testing and commissioning control systems for high-voltage substations? Would you like to apply your expertise to projects supporting Denmark’s electricity transmission grid? Join COWI as a Substation Control and Automation Specialist.

Develop and commission substation control systems

We are looking for an experienced specialist to work on control and automation systems for Energinet’s 132–400 kV substations. Projects range from new substations to extensions, refurbishment and replacement of systems at existing sites.

You will design, configure, test and commission substation control systems, including remote terminal units (RTUs), bay control units (BCUs) and human–machine interfaces (HMIs). • Configure, test and commission RTUs, bay control units and HMIs.

• Configure and verify communication interfaces between control devices, protection equipment and remote control systems.

• Plan and perform functional and integration testing to verify control functions, signal exchange and correct operation of system interfaces.

• Prepare and maintain configuration documentation, test procedures and test records.

Your expertise

You will also bring:

• A sound understanding of the interfaces between substation control systems, protection equipment and high-voltage primary equipment.

• Experience with functional testing, system integration and commissioning of substation control systems.

jobs.occupation: Senior Project Manager within Process Automation at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Does the idea of being part of the largest pharmaceutical projects in Denmark and managing complex Process Automation projects excite you? And do you thrive on defining and executing project strategies in close corporation with highly skilled colleagues? Then you’ll fit right in!

**Who We Are

**We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

**About The Role

**As a Senior Project Manager within Process Automation, you will be part of our large project portfolio in Kalundborg. You will play an important role in ensuring the successful execution of our deliveries and will be in close contact with both internal and external stakeholders.

As part of your role, you will maintain close dialogue with your team on-site and participate in regular meetings across disciplines, ensuring transparency, efficiency, and execution according to our plans.

The technical focus of this position is Process Automation, working with DCS 800xA and ECS solutions interfacing with new technologies within the Industry 4.0 domain and Manufacturing IT solutions. Our projects cover the entire project lifecycle, from conceptual and basic design phases to on-site testing activities, including FAT, Interface Testing, Wet Testing, SAT, and UAT, culminating in handover to our customers.

Based on your skills and experience, several opportunities are available within our portfolio.

Location Denmark - Kalundborg

Experience Minimum 5 Years

Department AIT Project Management

**How You Might Spend Your Days

**As a Project Manager, you will be responsible for:

• Executing projects within your area in close collaboration with your team, identifying risks and implementing mitigation measures.

• Focusing on overall project planning, ensuring delivery quality, and planning the necessary resources to maintain schedule and cost targets.

• Estimating costs and planning budgets in collaboration with our engineers and specialists.

• Managing project scope and ensuring that changes are analysed and agreed upon with stakeholders.

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• Work across the boundaries and you like to work in a diverse and international environment

• Create results through efficient project management and communication, leveraging from your relations to your team and stakeholder

• Have a personal commitment, known for your effectiveness and an open management style and know the impotency to win as a team

• Are fluent in English both written and spoken

**What You Bring To The Role

**To be successful in this role, we expect you to have the following experience and educational background:

• An educational background at bachelor's level or a similar relevant technical background.

• 6–10 years of experience with a proven track record in DCS and ECS/PLC Process Automation projects, preferably within the pharmaceutical industry.

• Experience with GMP project execution and preferable knowledge with S88 and S95

• Experience in executing Process Automation projects in collaboration with other disciplines, such as mechanical and process design, as well as end users.

• Experience with on-site commissioning activities, including FAT, SAT, and UAT.

• Project Management certification, e.g. PMP or PRINCE2, is preferred.

If you do not meet all the requirements, you are still welcome to apply and provide alternative experience that you believe would be valuable in this role.

Life at NNE NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, it means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer **here .

****Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Job Description Summary

The Production Engineer – Calibration & Maintenance is responsible for the calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle management of production, inspection, measurement, and test equipment used in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

The role works closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, equipment owners, and external service providers to ensure equipment remains calibrated, maintained, compliant, and available for production.

Responsibilities include day-to-day calibration and preventive maintenance coordination, HxGN EAM administration, calibration assessments, controlled procedures and work instructions, supplier coordination, and equipment compliance.

This is a hands-on Production Engineering role supporting manufacturing operations across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration/loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

Job Description

Roles & Responsibilities

• Coordinate the site calibration program, including calibration schedules, call-in activities, equipment status, due dates, and timely completion.

• Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including equipment preparation, shipment, return, documentation review, and release back to production.

• Ensure new, returned, overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment is appropriately assessed and controlled before use.

• Act as SME for calibration and maintenance activities in HxGN EAM, maintaining asset records, calibration setups, preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, task plans, and supporting documentation.

• Perform and support calibration assessments, including equipment requirements, criticality, acceptance criteria, calibration methods, frequencies, and maintenance needs.

• Develop and maintain calibration and maintenance procedures, SOPs, and work instructions in collaboration with equipment owners, SMEs, and Quality.

• Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for production and test equipment while minimizing disruption to manufacturing.

• Support investigations, risk assessments, and product-impact assessments related to overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment, and provide input to NC/INV/CAPA activities where applicable.

• Coordinate external calibration and maintenance suppliers, including quotations, service activities, documentation, and AGORA purchase orders.

• Support internal and external audits by ensuring calibration and maintenance records are complete, traceable, compliant, and audit-ready.

• Monitor calibration and maintenance performance and drive improvements in equipment compliance, availability, data quality, and execution efficiency.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Metrology, Maintenance, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience with calibration, preventive maintenance, equipment management, or Production Engineering in a regulated manufacturing environment.

• Understanding of calibration principles, equipment control, documentation, traceability, and manufacturing process requirements.

• Experience with computerized maintenance or Enterprise Asset Management systems, preferably HxGN EAM or comparable systems.

• Experience working within controlled procedures, work instructions, and change management processes.

• Experience coordinating suppliers, service activities, quotations, and purchase orders.

• Knowledge of GMP and Quality Management System requirements within regulated manufacturing.

Desired Characteristics

• Experience within medical device manufacturing or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.

• Hands-on and practical approach to supporting manufacturing equipment and production operations.

• Structured working style with strong ownership and ability to manage recurring deadlines.

• Strong collaboration skills across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and external suppliers.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfortable balancing equipment compliance, production continuity, quality requirements, and operational priorities.

• Proactive and improvement-focused approach to equipment reliability and calibration/maintenance processes

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead plays a key leadership role in overseeing Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs) while supporting the broader Clinical Trial Management (CTM) organization. This individual ensures high-quality clinical trial execution by providing strategic guidance, mentorship, and operational oversight. The Line Manager is responsible for team development, resource allocation, process optimization, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory standards. The Trial Delivery Team Lead may assume Global Trial Lead (GTL) responsibilities to address fluctuating demands.

**Roles & Responsibilities

****Leadership and Line Management:

**

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs), fostering professional growth.

• Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and identify training and career development opportunities.

• Ensure adequate resourcing, workload distribution, and succession planning within the team.

• Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the clinical operations team.

• Collaborate with Global Trial Leads (GTLs) on trial activities for assigned direct reports.

• Support trial deliverables by facilitating progress, coaching, and mentoring CTMs and CTAs.

• Advise on resource needs and support overall clinical trial resource planning.

• Ensure team success through setting clear expectations, guiding performance, and leading competency development.

• Lead functional working groups; serve as process owner or Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Operations.

• Support training initiatives across Trial Operations as needed.

• Collaborate with senior leadership to define and implement best practices within the Development Operations organization.

**Process & Compliance Management

**

• Ensure team adherence to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH guidelines, and regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, etc.).

• Develop and refine Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to optimize trial efficiency and compliance.

• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions by ensuring inspection readiness across clinical trials.

• Identify and drive process improvements to enhance trial execution and data quality.

• Lead cross-trial initiatives as needed, such as implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) or new process rollouts across the program.

• Manages the execution and implementation of CTM and CTA tasks, ensuring operational success.

• Initiates and supports the development of processes within the CTM and CTA group, focusing on practical application and continuous improvement.

• Collaborates across functions to drive efficiencies and provide day-to-day guidance to the CTM and CTA groups.

**Requirements – What You Must Have

**

• Bachelor of science degree with relevant specialization; Master of science degree preferred

• Minimum requirement of 12 or more years of experience in clinical operations

• Significant experience in leading and managing complex global clinical projects/programs

• Significant experience managing/guiding internal (cross-functional) and external (CRO, regulatory authorities) teams

• Experience with operational management and budget planning

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

• Global clinical program level experience required

• Experience within the field of oncology is preferred

• Minimum 2 years’ experience as Clinical Operations representative in Clinical Development Teams (CDTs) or Global Project Teams (GPTs) would be preferable

• Experience leading team members in global matrix environment, leveraging tools and technology to ensure business needs are met.

• Strategic thinking with ability to optimize organizational resources for successful program execution

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Moreover, You Meet The Following Personal Requirements

**

• Dedicated team player who enjoys leading teams and inspire trust among colleagues

• Quality mindset and able to prioritize your work in a fast paced and changing environment

• Result- and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$158,720.00---$238,080.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.
